title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, as inferred from the context pages. M is a module over a base S, probably of rank 2, since determinants appear. G = 𝔊(M) is a group scheme of linear automorphisms. 𝔼 (written 𝔼_S or 𝔼') is a group-like scheme, probably the multiplicative or additive line. ε_1 is some embedding 𝔼 → G, for instance an elementary or unipotent element, and ε_1(μ−1) is its value at μ−1. ρ and σ are two automorphisms acting on G. The notation is [α,ρ] := α ρ(α)^{-1}.

The 'loop equation' under study (82) is [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1(μ−1), with α, β sections of G and μ a section of 𝔼. 𝒢_{ρ,σ} is the scheme of its solutions (α, β, μ). The map (83), (α, β, μ) ↦ ([α,ρ], [β,σ], μ), sends 𝒢_{ρ,σ} to 𝒳_{ρ,σ}, the scheme of triples (x, y, μ) with x = y ε_1(μ−1) and x, y 'coboundaries'. The previous page states this map is an epimorphism.

This page makes it precise in three steps.

(i) There is a subscheme Ḃ'_0, coming from parts I–II of the notes. The map u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], det u) is an isomorphism Ḃ'_0 ≅ 𝒳_{ρ,σ}. So Ḃ'_0 is a slice, i.e. normal forms for the right-hand data.

(ii) u ↦ (u, u, det u) gives a section Ḃ'_0 → 𝒢_{ρ,σ} of (83). Its image is the 'diagonal' α = β: the pairs (u, μ) with u in Γℳ* and μ in Γ𝔼' satisfying (85) [u,ρ] = [u,σ] ε_1(μ−1). This forces μ = det u.

(iii) The general solution comes from twisted-conjugacy invariance. If a is fixed by ρ (a ∈ T_ρ, the fixed-point subgroup or stabilizer), then [u a^{-1}, ρ] = u a^{-1} ρ(a) ρ(u)^{-1} = [u,ρ]. Likewise for b ∈ T_σ.

Theorem (86)–(87), with (87) on the next page: the map B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ → G × G × 𝔼', (u, a, b) ↦ (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u), lands in 𝒢_{ρ,σ}, is a monomorphism, and is an isomorphism onto 𝒢_{ρ,σ}.

Equivalently, (88)–(90): every solution (α, β, μ) admits unique a ∈ T_ρ and b ∈ T_σ with αa and βb in B'_0. Then necessarily αa = βb =: u and μ = det u. Uniqueness is reduced to T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = T_σ ∩ B'_0 = {1}.

In modern terms: the fibres of the Lang-type map x ↦ x ρ(x)^{-1} are right cosets of the fixed-point subgroup scheme T_ρ. The solution scheme is therefore a product of a transversal (slice) B'_0 with two fixed-point groups. This is a non-abelian 1-coboundary / twisted-conjugacy computation, used to describe explicitly the solution scheme of the loop equation.
errors: This page writes the general solution as (u a, u b, det u), while (86) writes (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u). These are equivalent because T_ρ and T_σ are groups, so it is only a notational inconsistency.

Possible gap: the condition T_ρ ∩ B'_0 = {1} alone gives injectivity only if B'_0 is a subgroup, or under extra structure (e.g. B'_0 · T_ρ being a product decomposition). In general one needs each coset αT_ρ to meet B'_0 at most once. The text defers this to the explicit description in part II, so it may be fine there, but it is not justified on this page.
Existence of a and b with αa and βb in B'_0 and αa = βb relies on the surjectivity / isomorphism results of I–II, which are not visible here.

ideas.what: Fibres of the twisting map α ↦ α ρ(α)^{-1} are cosets of the fixed-point subgroup T_ρ. This is used to parametrise all solutions from a 'diagonal' section.
ideas.modern_name: Twisted conjugacy / Lang map; non-abelian coboundaries; fixed-point subgroup scheme
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard (Lang 1956 for the Lang map; Serre, Cohomologie galoisienne, for non-abelian H^1)
ideas.where_published: Group-scheme generalities of this kind are in SGA 3 in spirit; this specific computation is unpublished.

ideas.what: Product decomposition of the solution scheme of the loop equation as slice × T_ρ × T_σ, with a canonical section onto the diagonal α = β.
ideas.modern_name: Slice / transversal decomposition of a solution scheme (torsor-type description)
ideas.where_published: Not published; part of the unpublished 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' (1981 notes following La Longue Marche).

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine but careful explicit parametrisation of the solution scheme of a twisted-commutator equation in a linear group scheme. The key fact is that coboundaries are invariant under right multiplication by fixed points. Its interest lies only in its place within the unpublished 'équation des lacets' programme, not in any new idea on this page.
transcription_corrections: Top of page: '444' is the author's page number in Grothendieck's own pagination.
'qu'on trouve [?] de déterminer aussi' most likely reads 'qu'on vient de déterminer aussi'.
The diagram's vertical arrow from Ḃ'_0 to 𝒳_{ρ,σ} is marked as an isomorphism. The section Ḃ'_0 → 𝒢_{ρ,σ} is the diagonal arrow, given by u ↦ (u, u, det u).
In (86) the image is (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u), with exponents −1 on a and b, matching (89) on the next page.
